title: Quasi-splitting and regular constants preserve evaluation alterations
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $Y$ a normal projective geometrically integral finite-type $k$-scheme, $C$ an integral proper finite-type $k$-scheme, and $g:C\to Y$ a proper dominant morphism. Let $S$ be normal integral projective of finite type over $k$, $b_0:S\to Y$ an equivariant alteration, and $(W\xrightarrow{w}S,s_i)$ an H-projective stable pointed curve with smooth geometrically integral generic fibre. Suppose $W$ is integral and there is an equivariant dominant morphism $a_0:W\to C$ with $ga_0=b_0w$ and finite function-field extension $k(W)/k(C)$. Let finite groups $J,H$ have a surjection $\beta:J\to H$, with compatible actions on $k,S,W,C,Y$ through $\beta$ where appropriate, and with the union of sections stable under $J$. Put $A_0=\ker\beta$, $K=k(Y)$, $F=k(C)$, and assume $k(S)^{A_0}/K$ and $k(W)^{A_0}/F$ are purely inseparable.

There are a finite group $G$ with a surjection $\rho:G\to J$, a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme $S_4$, an equivariant finite surjective generically etale morphism $S_4\to S$, a finite field extension $e/k$ with a $G$-action, and a normal projective geometrically integral finite-type $e$-scheme $B$ with compatible $G$-action and an equivariant finite radicial surjection $B\to S_4$. Put $\alpha=\beta\rho$ and $A=\ker\alpha$. The pulled-back family $v:V=W\times_S B\to B$ is integral, H-projective and stable pointed, with smooth geometrically integral generic fibre and quasi-split nodal fibres. Its pulled-back sections remain disjoint and smooth, with $G$-stable union. One has $k(S_4)^{\ker\rho}=k(S)$, $k(B)/k(S_4)$ finite purely inseparable, and $e^A/k$, $k(B)^A/K$, $k(V)^A/F$ purely inseparable. The action on $e$ extends the one on $k$ via $\alpha$. The composites $b:B\to Y$ and $c:V\to C$ are equivariant H-projective surjective alterations, and $gc=bv$. In particular each is finite over some dense open of its target. If $\dim Y=0$, then $B=\operatorname{Spec}e$. Radicial means universally injective; generically etale means etale over a dense open, using [def-weil-etale-morphism].

Field, integrality, properness, finite type, geometric integrality, dimension, H-projectivity, finite morphisms, surjectivity, function fields and field extensions use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-pc-field-tower]. H-projective means a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target. Normal means all local rings are integrally closed domains. An alteration is a proper surjective morphism of integral schemes, with finite function-field extension and finite over a dense open. Actions may be nonfaithful and semilinear on the ground field; equivariance through a group surjection always includes its action on that field. Purely inseparable means every element has a characteristic-power in the smaller field in positive characteristic, and equality in characteristic zero. Flatness, finite presentation, smoothness, geometric fibres, closed immersions and fibre products use [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-pc-fibre-product]. Stable pointed curve means [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve]; its sections may be permuted. Quasi-split means [def-sfb-quasi-split-nodal-fibres].

source.place: Lemmas 5.5 and 5.7, pp.614--615, and §3.11; returned proof Steps 9--11, finite quasi-splitting, radicial constants and H-projective graph alterations. Local PDF WANTED; publisher scan consulted online.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-finite-quasi-splitting] to $W\to S$ with the acting group $J$. Its hypotheses follow from [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve] and the assumed H-projectivity and smooth geometrically integral generic fibre. Obtain $r:S_4\to S$ and $\rho:G\twoheadrightarrow J$ with $S_4$ normal integral projective, $r$ finite surjective generically etale, and $L_4^N=L$, where $L=k(S)$, $L_4=k(S_4)$, $N=\ker\rho$. The pulled-back family $W_4=W\times_S S_4$ has quasi-split fibres. Set $\alpha=\beta\rho$ and $A=\ker\alpha$. On every pullback use the diagonal action; on a pair $(x,t)$ it is $g(x,t)=(\rho(g)x,gt)$.

source.place: Lemma 5.7, printed pp.614--615, with the stable-curve hypotheses expanded

proof.text: The finite dominant $r$ gives $[L_4:L]<\infty$: over a nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, its inverse image is affine with domain coordinate ring $R'$ finite over $R$; use [lem-trf-finite-domain-fraction-degree] and [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. Since $b_0$ is finite over a dense open of $Y$, $b_4=b_0r$ is finite over that same open by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. It is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](c), surjective since both factors are, and has finite function-field extension by the finite tower $K\subset L\subset L_4$. Thus $b_4:S_4\to Y$ is an equivariant alteration.

source.place: Lemma 5.7 followed by the alteration composition in Remarks 2.3(iii)

proof.text: Put $D=k(W)$. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-curve-pullback-function-field] to $W\to S$ and $S_4\to S$. Flatness, reduced geometric fibres and dominance follow from the stable-curve conditions (the fibres are nonempty); the generic fibre is geometrically integral by hypothesis. It gives $W_4$ integral and $D_4=k(W_4)=D\otimes_L L_4$, finite over $D$. For later field calculations, $D\otimes_L T$ is a domain for every extension $T/L$: choose a nonempty affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R$ in the geometrically integral generic fibre. By [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], $R\otimes_L T$ is a domain. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $D=\operatorname{Frac}R$, so $D\otimes_L T$ is the localization of $R\otimes_L T$ at $R\setminus\{0\}$, a multiplicative set avoiding zero. This also proves the same assertion for $D_4/L_4$ using its geometrically integral generic fibre.

source.place: Theorem 5.9 proof, printed p.617, ordinary fibre products; explicit generic-field verification

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-curve-field-kernel-invariant-tower] with $L,D,L'=L_4,J'=G,\rho$, the given $\beta:J\to H$, and the subfields $K=k(Y)$ and $F=k(C)$. Step 3 checks its domain hypothesis for every field extension; Step 2 checks finiteness, and Step 1 gives $(L')^N=L$, hence the required purely inseparable fixed-field extension. The assumed $L^{A_0}/K$ and $D^{A_0}/F$ are precisely its two remaining hypotheses. The conclusion is $L_4^A/K$ and $D_4^A/F$ purely inseparable. The tensor action is the action induced by the diagonal scheme action, because on products of pulled-back rational functions it sends $d\otimes l$ to $\rho(g)d\otimes gl$.

source.place: Remarks 2.3(iii) and the Galois-theory verification following Lemma 5.5; existing kernel-invariant lemma

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-alteration-constant-regularization] to $b_4:S_4\to Y$ and $\alpha:G\to H$. Step 2 gives an alteration, Step 1 gives normal integral projective finite-type $S_4$, and Step 4 gives $L_4^A/K$ purely inseparable. All hypotheses on $Y/k$ are given. Obtain $e/k$, $B/e$ and $q:B\to S_4$, with the same group $G$, as in that lemma. In particular $q$ is finite radicial surjective, $M=k(B)$ is finite purely inseparable over $L_4$, $e^A/k$ and $M^A/K$ are purely inseparable, $b=b_4q$ is H-projective, and $\dim Y=0$ implies $B=\operatorname{Spec}e$. Its action on $e$ extends the original action on $k$, which factors through $\alpha$.

source.place: Lemma 5.5, printed p.614, geometric reduction and Stein constants over the field base

proof.text: The composite $B\to S$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition], so it is dominant (it is surjective), with finite function-field extension $M/L$. The scheme $B$ is H-projective over $k$: compose the H-projective $b$ of Step 5 with $Y/k$, using [lem-trf-h-projective-composition]. It is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-curve-pullback-function-field] to $W/S$ and $B\to S$. This gives the ordinary pullback $V=W\times_S B$ integral, with $k(V)=D\otimes_L M$ finite over $D$. Associativity of tensor products identifies this field with $D_4\otimes_{L_4}M$, by $(d\otimes l)\otimes m\mapsto d\otimes lm$. Apply [lem-sfb-curve-field-kernel-invariant-tower] a second time to $L_4,D_4,M$, with the identity group surjection $G\to G$ and the map $\alpha:G\to H$. Here the new kernel is $\ker(\mathrm{id}_G)=\{1\}$, so its fixed field is $M$ itself; hence the kernel-fixed-field hypothesis is exactly the finite purely inseparable extension $M/L_4$ from Step 5. The further kernel stays $A=\ker\alpha$. Step 3 gives the domain hypothesis for $D_4/L_4$, and Step 4 gives both old invariant hypotheses. It follows that $k(V)^A/F$ is purely inseparable.

source.place: Theorem 5.9 proof, printed p.617, final pullback; Lemma 5.5 purely inseparable extension

proof.text: Pull the sections to $V/B$. The arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-stable-pointed-generic-extension] preserves all stable pointed conditions, including disjoint smooth sections, also with no markings. Their union stays $G$-stable: $g(s_i(t),t)=(s_{\rho(g)i}(gt),gt)$. The arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-nodal-finite-quasi-splitting], applied first over $S_4$, preserves quasi-splitting after $q$. The generic fibre is the old smooth geometrically integral curve extended from $L$ to $M$; its smoothness follows from the dominant-base-change clause of [lem-trf-semistable-marked-base-change] and its geometric integrality from Step 6. H-projectivity of $v$ follows by [lem-pc-projective-base-change].

source.place: Lemma 5.7 and Theorem 5.9 proof, printed pp.615,617; stable marked base change

proof.text: The maps $b:B\to Y$ (Step 5) and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are H-projective. Twice applying [lem-trf-h-projective-composition], also to $v$, gives an embedding $i:V\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_k$. Define $c=a_0\operatorname{pr}_W:V\to C$. Since $C/k$ is proper it is separated, by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-change-of-base-closed-immersion] with $X=V$, $T=C$, the two maps $c$ and $\mathrm{id}_C$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$: the graph $V=V\times_C C\to V\times_k C$ is a closed immersion. Follow it by $i\times\mathrm{id}_C$, a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Composition is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp], and [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback] identifies its target with $\mathbf P^n_C$. Its projection is $c$, so $c$ is H-projective. This is a two-embedding argument; it assumes no projectivity of $C/k$.

source.place: Tags 01KR (schemes-lemma-fibre-product-after-map), 01QR and 01QS; projective graph argument of §3.11

proof.text: Both $b,c$ are proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]. They are dominant: $b$ is a composite of surjections, while $c$ has the injective field map $F\hookrightarrow D\hookrightarrow k(V)$ from Step 6. Their function-field extensions are finite, respectively the tower $K\subset L\subset L_4\subset M$ and $F\subset D\subset k(V)$. Their images are closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image]; a closed dense image is the whole integral target, so both are surjective. To check the dense-open finiteness explicitly, take a nonempty affine target open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ for either map; $R$ is a Noetherian domain by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Its generic fibre has dimension zero: every nonempty affine chart of that fibre has a coordinate domain contained in the finite extension of target function fields. Every element is algebraic over the target field; a nonzero element has inverse given by its minimal polynomial with nonzero constant term, so that chart is a field. Now [lem-fin-projective-generically-finite], applied after restriction (projectivity persists by [lem-pc-projective-base-change]), gives finiteness over a nonempty open. This open is dense in the integral target. Thus $b,c$ are alterations in the stipulated sense.

All composites are equivariant by their construction. For the two projections of $V=W\times_S B$, the defining equality is $w\operatorname{pr}_W=(B\to S)v$. Composing $ga_0=b_0w$ with $\operatorname{pr}_W$ therefore gives $gc=bv$. The finite-cover fixed field $k(S_4)^{\ker\rho}=k(S)$ is Step 1; the three purely inseparable invariant extensions and the radicial field extension are Steps 4--6; all family properties are Step 7. The zero-dimensional assertion is the last clause supplied in Step 5. These are exactly the asserted data and conclusions.
